- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.16), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to counteract bias.  
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (especially >80); apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.  
- If last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (price dropping from 80+), model tends to ignore it; adjust downward by 2–4% for next 3 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; use 14-day moving average of true prices as baseline for smoothing.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid “sentiment lag” bias.
